architectureFinding.finding: Resolver-v3 prospective card used L0 fallback/C1 probabilities while richer HBT-1.4 intelligence families exist separately. Forensic evidence indicates availability, confirmed-XI, goalkeeper, set-piece and tactical state should be surfaced alongside L0 rather than discarded or silently converted into unvalidated probability weights.
architectureFinding.action: Add non-destructive intelligence-overlay surfacing. Keep base HDA frozen; expose risk/support factors and require historical validation before any factor changes probability.

prematchKnowableEvidence.evidence: Omar El Hilali was suspended after a direct red in the previous match, forcing a defensive change.
Edu Exposito was returning after missing the previous match with physical discomfort; Andoni Gorosabel had also been managing discomfort.
Jofre Carreras remained unavailable with pubic discomfort.

postMatchEvidence.evidence: Elche were reduced to ten men in the 6th minute, yet scored twice before the half-hour. Espanyol later hit the woodwork and created further chances before Elche sealed the game on a counter.

Post-match player review described Dmitrovic as again making costly errors after a poor prior outing. This is post-match commentary, so it is a hypothesis source; only prior-match goalkeeper evidence may be used causally.

cases.conclusion: Do not retune from this case. The result contains both knowable pre-match availability signals and substantial match-level variance/process evidence. Backtest candidate factors before promotion.

prematchKnowableEvidence.evidence: Sassuolo defender Jay Idzes was unavailable with a moderate left-quadriceps injury. Other reported unavailable/doubtful players included Pieragnolo, Cande, Ismael Kone, Walukiewicz, Volpato and Paz.
prematchKnowableEvidence.source: La Gazzetta dello Sport probable formations, updated 17 Sep 2026

prematchKnowableEvidence.evidence: ANSA's pre-match report independently noted Idzes' moderate quadriceps injury and expected a replacement in central defence.

postMatchEvidence.evidence: Monza's report described an aggressive start and sustained pressure, with Sassuolo struggling to play out of it.
Monza's first goal came from a corner sequence with Varela unmarked and goalkeeper Muric failing to claim cleanly; the second came from a penalty.

cases.conclusion: This is a stronger candidate for a missed pre-match state signal than Espanyol. Do not alter probability from one case; first test defensive-absence clusters and tactical press-resistance historically.
